articles.title: Letter: the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center Did a Good Job This Winter
body: To the editor: I have lived on Coal Court for 16 years, and I want to say what a difference the Hickory Ridge Recreation Center has made.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the September meeting.
Dominic Emerson, Tannery Flats

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Elementary Adds Community Oven to Summer Schedule
articles.deck: The program begins in February and is open to all students in grade 3 and up.
body: Students will meet on Saturday afternoons in the Cedar Hollow Pavilion, and transportation will be provided for those who need it. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for February.
Principal Dominic Farrow said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers. The board will review the results at the end of the summer term.

body: The effort began in January when a handful of neighbors met at the Cedar Hollow Pavilion to talk about seasonal farmers market. The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
The Foxglove Heights Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings.

articles.deck: Friends remember Simone Mahoney for the many years of service to Bellwood.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Bellwood. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Upper Commons Historical Society in his or her name.
